findings: The assembled candidate shows separate cap/body side and roof cleats with rivets, packing strips and detachable bolt/nut/lockwasher sets.

The actual world-coordinate detail crop shows the middle roof rivet displaced transversely from the bolt and nut. The prior centered pattern and its four measured intersections remain preserved in casing_cap_build.

The reopened fixture contains661 valid single-solid leaves,94 newly added. All914 new/changed material candidate pairs,50 receiving bores,50 joint-seating checks and14 cylindrical-envelope retention checks pass.

The side bolts project1.9mm beyond the assumed nuts; the roof bolts project2.9mm. Nut bores have0.1mm radial clearance around the simplified bolt envelopes. Threads, spring action, clamp loads and tool access are not qualified.

Fourteen three-part detachable sets follow SNL31:002. Original SNL128 and270 support independent plain-nut and lockwasher identities. Cleat shapes, stock, packing location and hole coordinates remain documented reconstruction assumptions.

The candidate has12 short and6 long cleat rivets per casing. Adding existing17 wall-angle short rivets fills the body26 short allocation; cap3 short allocation is also filled. Cap/body long-rivet and global catalogue conflicts remain unresolved.
Register plates, beading, support brackets and remaining fastening still require geometry. The casing study remains isolated from the standard tank.
